look_here_first: Find the FLOWER CLUSTER where it meets an opposite-leaf node. Talayote has MANY very small (~5 mm wide) pale yellow-green flowers with WHITISH petal margins on a branching/racemelike AXILLARY cyme; larger Matelea milkvines have much showier netted or longitudinally striped flowers. An older plump smooth green follicle (7.5–9.5 cm long) and a line of short hairs running along each internode give excellent confirmation.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Perennial vigorous herbaceous twining vine with white milky latex; many stems may arise from base

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Stems usually cylindrical, tough, slender ~2 mm diameter, short-hairy, hairs often arranged as a LINE along each internode

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaves opposite/decussate with petioles ~10–55 mm; blades deeply heart-shaped at base, often ~2–10 cm long with acute to acuminate tips

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Axillary many-flowered racemelike cyme, often 10 or more tiny flowers, with secondary 1–2-flowered cymules and zigzag rachis

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Flowers about 5 mm across, green-yellow with thin white margin around short petals, not the showy dark reticulate large green Matelea stars

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Corolla campanulate-rotate, lobes ~3 mm, bearing inner marginal ridges; corona of five fleshy segments, 3-lobed near apex

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Fruit large PLUMP smooth glabrous green follicle, not muricate, ~75–95 mm x 30–33 mm; commonly blunt toward tip

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Seeds flattened with brown winged margins and a tuft of white silky coma hairs

key_traits.label: Phenology
key_traits.text: Regional flowering typically late spring into fall; field photo date and local weather should be considered.

key_traits.label: Leaf venation
key_traits.text: Principal veins conspicuous and raised below; heart-shaped leaf form overlaps Matelea, Gonolobus and certain other Apocynaceae.

key_traits.label: Latex caution
key_traits.text: White latex also occurs in Matelea and other milkvines; it is not a safe stand-alone genus discriminator.
